messages:
Emma H: FYI support escalation from AcmeApp — intermittent SSE streams end with partial JSON. Customer says client receives valid chunks then a connection close and the JSON is left incomplete (no finish_reason). They see parser errors client-side.

Charlie K: CRITICAL for them — production traffic. Any quick repro?

Emma H: They sent a sample capture. Here's the tail of the stream they got: 

```
data: {"id":"tok_abc","object":"response","choices":[{"index":0,"text":"...\n  }], "usage":{"prompt_tokens":120,"completion_tokens":45}, "finish_reason":

# connection closed by server abruptly (client shows ECONNRESET)
```

Client reports reconnects immediately but when they stitch responses they get invalid JSON. No finish_reason present in the last emitted event.

Jenna (CS): Customer also mentioned the issue got worse during a deploy window yesterday, and that they rotate tokens every 10m which sometimes causes short reconnects.

Liu W: thanks — do we have server logs for that timeframe? Any gateway 502/499?

Emma H: Pasted below from our edge logs (trimmed):

```
[edge-2026-03-14T21:04:12Z] conn=98765 req_id=xyz stream_write_chunk len=512
[edge-2026-03-14T21:04:12Z] conn=98765 req_id=xyz stream_write_chunk len=128
[edge-2026-03-14T21:04:12Z] conn=98765 req_id=xyz client_closed_early ECONNRESET
[runtime-2026-03-14T21:04:12Z] req_id=xyz worker=gw-7 status=200 bytes_sent=640
```

Ben R: That pattern looks like the last small chunk got sent then the client closed before we finished flushing the final JSON object. Could be a proxy/keepalive cutoff or client-side token rotation reconnect.

Liu W: Two hypotheses: (1) edge/proxy is closing idle SSE conn due to keepalive/idle timeout while we wait on a long model decode; (2) client attempts to resume by opening a new connection and our server doesn't support resume, so the client concatenates two half-objects, producing invalid JSON.

Charlie K: Any client repro we can run locally? Customer provided a curl capture.

Emma H: Repro curl they used (they said reliably repro when model latency spikes):

```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=test-llm" --verbose
```

When latency goes high, connection stays open and we stream partial tokens. If connection cuts, curl shows truncated final event.

Liu W: Let's try a local repro that simulates a sudden TCP RST after the server writes a partial chunk. I can write a tiny script to accept an SSE and close socket mid-fragment.

Ben R: Also check our proxy (nginx) config: proxy_read_timeout, proxy_send_timeout, proxy_buffering. If proxy buffers too much or times out, could tear the connection leaving partial chunk delivered. On the runtime side, we normally set proxy_send_timeout=300s but sometimes a mis-deployed change set it down.

sre-bot: NOTE: recent infra deploy yesterday changed nginx-worker-timeout on edge pool 3 — roll ID infra-2026-03-14T20:58.

Ben R: that correlates with the customer's window. Good catch. If the worker timeouts are shorter than idle decode periods, nginx may force-close.

Charlie K: What about the absent finish_reason? Should finish_reason be emitted in a separate final event? If the final event didn't make it to the client because of early close, they won't see it.

Liu W: Correct — our streaming contract sends final event with metadata including finish_reason, stop tokens, and closing JSON punctuation. If that event is dropped mid-flight, client JSON is incomplete.

Emma H: Customer also shared that their client tries to reconnect using a resume token in a custom header X-Last-Event-Id. We don't accept resume tokens today, so on reconnect they get a new stream from scratch and naively concat, causing invalid JSON.

Jenna (CS): Ok so two failure modes: server/proxy cut leaves truncated fragment; client reconnects and stitches streams without proper resume semantics. Both make final JSON invalid.

Ben R: Short term mitigations: 
- Ask customer to treat each SSE data: event as an independent JSON object (not concatenating streams), or buffer and parse robustly until a full JSON parse succeeds.
- On our side: revert the nginx worker-timeout change on edge pool 3 to previous values and ensure proxy_send_timeout >= model max decode time.

Liu W: Medium-term: implement a small end-of-stream marker event that is a guaranteed standalone line (e.g., data: {"redwood_stream_end":true}), so clients can rely on it even if the last partial typed tokens were dropped. Also add an optional resume token protocol for deterministic resumption.

Ben R: Lower-risk immediate action: ensure runtime flushes the final event with a short keepalive ping immediately before we close the app-level connection to minimize race. Also add server-side retries on transient ECONNRESET during final flush.

Emma H: I've asked infra to roll back the timeout change and posted steps. infra assigned to @Ben R.

deploy-bot: deployment infra-rollback-367 initiated by Ben R.

Ben R: I'll monitor edge logs for the customer req_id xyz after rollback. If we still see truncated streams, we'll open a dedicated runtime ticket to add the end-of-stream marker.

Liu W: I'll prototype a tiny test harness that simulates delayed final flush and a mid-fragment close — will push to https://git.redwood.ai/eng-runtime/stream-repro (private) and attach instructions.

Charlie K: Action items summary for support thread: 
- Emma: send customer mitigation steps (treat SSE events as self-contained, small client-side parser changes).
- Ben: rollback infra timeout and confirm.
- Liu: create repro harness and propose end-of-stream marker and resume protocol.
- Jenna: keep customer posted and request logs if issue recurs.

Emma H: I've sent the mitigation note to AcmeApp and opened ticket RWD-9876 (P1) tracking rollback + runtime follow-up. Customer appreciated the quick turnaround.

Jenna (CS): :thumbsup: good work.

Ben R: Monitoring window 2h after rollback. I'll update thread with outcomes.

Liu W: If anyone can review the prototype once it's up I'd appreciate it — will ping.

Emma H: closing loop for now — will post updates.

Charlie K: thx all.
